body.statement: For every legal \(q_\star\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\), the following are equivalent: \(S\) is Hausdorff continuous at \(q_\star\) relative to \(\overline{\mathcal Q}\); for every feasible nonzero face \(F\in\mathfrak F(q_\star)\), \[S(q_\star)=\bigcup_{\gamma\in J_F}S_\gamma(q_\star);\] and there exist \(\varepsilon,H>0\) such that \[d_H(S(q),S(q_\star))\le H\|q-q_\star\|\] for every \(q\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\) with \(\|q-q_\star\|<\varepsilon\).
body.justification: The theorem gives a finite observable-law frontier separating regular and discontinuous sharp policy sets.
body.gap: Beresteanu--Molinari and Chernozhukov--Hong--Tamer do not treat components whose feasibility domains disappear inside a nonconvex union.
body.consumer: The criterion determines when a regular plug-in policy-set analysis is locally defensible and when global inversion is required.
